mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed policy cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such events (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.0% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism.
regime_hint: high unemployment or weak wage growth regime
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant during such UNRATE spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) by at least 3% in the two months prior to the decision are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% in each of the two prior months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying HOUST momentum (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 2% followed by a rebound in the next month creates a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of soft supply growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in month t, then rises in month t+1
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or are not statistically significant during such INDPRO patterns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return as markets anticipate continued accommodative policy and lower rates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 150,000 in a month triggers a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates labor market weakness.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or not statistically significant during such events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly GDP demand proxies (GDPC1) above 20,000 million chained dollars in the prior quarter is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such GDPC1 spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in RSAFS (retail sales) followed by a sustained rise for three months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects a bottoming-out in weak retail demand cycles.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for two months then rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such RSAFS patterns (p > 0.05).
